title: The hole through the mountain
learning_goal: Know that the Fréjus tunnel was dug from both ends between 1857 and 1870, opened thirteen months before Fogg's train, and was the longest in the world until 1882 — and that a machine is why it took thirteen years, not seventy-one.

narration.script:
That was the way over. This is the way through.

They started in 1857, from both ends, with nothing in the middle: no shaft, no daylight, two teams walking towards each other under the mountain. By hand, people said, it would have taken about seventy-one years.

So Germain Sommeiller's men used a machine he had to invent first — a compressed-air drill, ten of them held in one frame. And the air that drove the drills came out of them and became the air the men breathed.

The two ends met on the twenty-sixth of December, 1870. The tunnel opened on the seventeenth of September, 1871 — thirteen months before Fogg's train. Nobody had ever made a hole this long, and nobody made a longer one until 1882.

And here it is today. Italians call it simply il traforo — the tunnel. Same arch, same hole, still the way through.

production_notes: SEGMENT 5, second third (85 s; 154 words of the segment's 385). This is the chapter's one genuinely information-dense beat and it sits at the density ceiling, so every number that a caption or the next scene's diagram carries is NOT read aloud (R3): the length, the mean altitude, the air pressure and the hole count are on captions; '13 years, not 71' is a callout on G-202 in the next scene, so the guide says the seventy-one only once, here, hedged as 'reportedly' exactly as F-71 hedges it. NO SUPERLATIVE PILE-UP on F-70: 'nobody had ever made a hole in the world this long, and nobody made a longer one until 1882' — plainly, once. THE GLOSS CHIP IS EARNED: the guide says 'il traforo' out loud at ~66 s. M-205 (the CC BY 3.0 drone footage of the Alps) is deliberately NOT in this scene: it is winter footage and Fogg crosses in early October, and the player cannot show `footage` anyway; if the linear cut wants the mass of the mountain, use 0:15-0:30 or 4:15-4:30 with the burn-in 'Electric Life · CC BY 3.0 · trimmed' and never under a line about the season. M-206 (the Fréjus ROAD tunnel drive, 1980) is rejected — same mountain, wrong hole (rundown Decision 6).
